$comment: Hand-written, not generated. The one push contract every sender (gateway plugin, Hermie Web, the relay) and both app generations conform to. See contract/README.md.

legacyTypes.$comment: Still valid on the wire because older registrations and senders carry it; no current sender produces it and no app offers a switch for it.

category.$comment: An action is a hint, never an instruction: the app re-reads the open request by requestId and answers only if it is still open and still says what the notification said.

android.$comment: Channel id equals the type name, one channel per type.

data.$comment: The notification's data bag. Everything here is resolved against the gateway on tap; nothing in it is acted on unverified. Optional fields are omitted, never sent empty or null.

fields.description: The profile name of the bot whose chat this is.
The session the event happened in. Present whenever the event has a session; omitted otherwise.
Legacy spelling of sessionId, written by Hermie Web for older app builds. Readers prefer sessionId.
Which kind of conversation the session is.
The server request the notification was raised for. Required for an approval, which the Allow and Deny actions answer; a clarify carries it when the sender knows it.
type request only: the server request method (approval, clarify, ...).
Present (true) when the event happened inside a scheduled run.
false: the cron attribution is a guess, word it as a plain message. Absent: treat as certain.
The scheduler's job id. Carried, never shown: no title or body contains it.
gatewayKeyOf(the gateway origin): FNV-1a 64 of the origin; see contract/gateway/vectors/gateway-key.json.

A stable id for the one fact the notification is about: '<kind>:' plus the first 32 hex digits of SHA-256 over the UTF-8 of Python's json.dumps(parts) (ensure_ascii, ', ' separators), where parts are the event's identity (for an approval: session id, request id). Two senders describing the same fact from the same ids arrive at the same string. A relay sender uses it as the collapse id.
The payload version. Written by the gateway plugin; readers do not require it.
Unix seconds when the event happened. Written by the gateway plugin; informational.
